texts.preamble: Mahipal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 7 December, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:232539 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1134 of 2009 Revisionist :- Mahipal Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Ashish Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: The facts of the case are that the complainant Umesh Prasad Gupta, Food Inspector stopped the revisionist on 28.3.1996 at about 11.30 a.m. at Ilahibagh, Behrampur, P.S.- Tiwaripur, Gorakhpur while he was carrying milk in two containers which was intended for sale. On suspicion of it being adulterated, he disclosed his identity to the accused and asked license for sale to which he denied. The complainant purchased 660ml milk by giving Rs.6/-for sample and then kept in three bottles in equal quantity in which 18 drops of formalin each was added for preserving it which was then sent to the public analyst for chemical analysis who vide his report being report no. 2878 dated 10.5.1996 reported it to be adulterated as it contained 42 per cent less milk fat and 29 percent less milk solid non-fat in it. The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused. In the trial court the complainant Umesh Prasad Gupta, Food Inspector, was examined as P.W.-1 and Wali Mohammad, retired Office Superintendent, was examined as P.W.-2. The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that Mr. Umesh Prasad Gupta, Food Inspector, was examined as PW-1 under Section 246 Cr.P.C. and states of taking sample of mixed milk from container allegedly belonging to the revisionist. It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the said material was stirred and homogenized before taking sample of milk. It is further argued that in so far as the milk is concerned the sample has to be taken after stirring and homogenizing of material as the fat in the milk gets settled in bottom being heavy. It is argued that in view of the said discrepancy the revisionist cannot be stated to be carrying milk which was deficient in milk fat and milk fat not solid. It is argued that since the material was not stirred and homogenized before taking its sample and launch of the prosecution on an erroneous report of the Food Analyst, the present revision deserves to be allowed. 7. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.
